papers.title: Synthetic Demo Paper A: Mesoporous TiO2 Electron Transport Layers
Synthetic Demo Paper B: SnO2 versus TiO2 ETLs under Damp-Heat

paragraphs.text: In this work we fabricate perovskite solar cells using a mesoporous TiO2 electron transport layer deposited by spin-coating.
The champion device reaches a power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 21.1% under AM 1.5G illumination at 100 mW cm-2.
Chen et al. previously reported that TiO2-based devices degrade under ultraviolet illumination, which motivated our UV-filtering encapsulation.
We compare titanium dioxide (TiO2) and SnO2 electron transport layers in perovskite solar cells subjected to damp-heat ageing at 85 C and 85% relative humidity.
After 500 hours, the SnO2 devices retain 92% of their initial PCE, whereas the TiO2 devices retain only 74%.
All devices in this study were prepared by spin-coating, consistent with common practice in the field.
